rationale: C10 is an essentially verbatim prior-year version of the child directive. It designates the same person, holding the same judicial office, to exercise the same District Court duties under the same triggering conditions and compensation rule; the material substantive change is only the concluding year, from 1955 to 1956. C14 is the corresponding 1954 version, while C15 is a slightly earlier version with minor differences in Snyder's title and the court's styling.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby designate and authorize the Honorable A. Cecil Snyder, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby designate and authorize the Honorable A. Cecil Snyder, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico
shared_material.explanation: Identical opening designation of the same official in the same capacity.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to perform and discharge the duties of the office of Judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico, and to sign all necessary papers and records as acting judge of the said district court, without extra compensation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: to perform and discharge the duties of the office of Judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico, and to sign all necessary papers and records as acting judge of the said district court, without extra compensation
shared_material.explanation: The operative authority and administrative machinery are reproduced verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: in case of vacancy in the office of judge of the said district court, or in case of the death, absence, illness, or other legal disability of the judge thereof, during the year 1956
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in case of vacancy in the office of judge of the said district court, or in case of the death, absence, illness, or other legal disability of the judge thereof, during the year 1955
shared_material.explanation: The same complete set of triggering conditions is retained, with only the annual authorization date updated.
